title: Georgakopoulos–Papasoglu fat minor conjecture
statement:
Let $X$ and $G$ be graphs, let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ be a function. A graph is **$K$-fat-minor-free with respect to $X$** when it does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor.

**Fat minor conjecture.** For every graph $X$ there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}^2$ such that, for every graph $G$ and $K\in\mathbb{N}$, if $G$ does not contain $X$ as a $K$-fat minor, then $G$ is $f(K)$-quasi-isometric to a graph with no $X$ minor.

This conjecture has been disproved, with further counterexamples showing failure even for certain small graphs and under a weakened conclusion. It is therefore refuted rather than open.
source_name: Sandra Albrechtsen, “A coarse Menger theorem for hyperbolic graphs, finitely presented groups, and more”, arXiv:2606.17605 (2026).
references:
**12 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2601.05761](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05761), [arXiv:2510.14644](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14644), [arXiv:2508.15342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15342), [arXiv:2412.15675](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15675), [arXiv:2408.10748](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.10748), [arXiv:2408.15335](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15335), [arXiv:2406.07802](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07802), [arXiv:2405.17218](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17218), [arXiv:2405.09383](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09383), [arXiv:2312.08902](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08902), [arXiv:2310.15242](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15242).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2026). “Davies, Hickingbotham, Illingworth, and McCarty .”
